response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT ci.location, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId = q.raceId JOIN circuits ci ON ci.circuitId = r.circuitId GROUP BY ci.location), s AS (SELECT location, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), t AS (SELECT location, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT location, cnt AS qualifying_count, share, share - avg_share AS share_above_average FROM t WHERE share > avg_share ORDER BY share DESC

assumptions.assumption: Cities are the distinct values of circuits.location. Circuits that share a location text are combined into one city.

The average share is taken over cities that have at least one qualifying record. That is the same as 1 divided by the number of such cities. Cities with no qualifying records are left out of the average.
'How far above' is the plain difference share - average share. It is not a ratio.

alternatives.interpretation: The average share also counts cities that have no qualifying records, each with a count of 0. The average then becomes 1 divided by the number of all distinct locations.
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT ci.location, COUNT(q.qualifyId) AS cnt FROM circuits ci LEFT JOIN races r ON r.circuitId = ci.circuitId LEFT JOIN qualifying q ON q.raceId = r.raceId GROUP BY ci.location), s AS (SELECT location, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), t AS (SELECT location, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT location, cnt AS qualifying_count, share, share - avg_share AS share_above_average FROM t WHERE share > avg_share ORDER BY share DESC
